scope: Source-only bounded ARC storage/init audit using already retained Kubernetes metadata; no new runtime observation.
finding: No actionable source-supported PVC, mount configuration, init ordering or avoidable pre-ready reliability defect was established for the observed mount deadlines.

verifiedContracts.evidence: Both templates define one generic ephemeral 100Gi ReadWriteOnce filesystem PVC using rook-ceph-block, preserving per-Pod isolation.

verifiedContracts.contract: Matching storage class and mount admission
verifiedContracts.evidence: Source rook-ceph-block selects ext4 with noatime and the existing RBD CSI provisioner. Init requires an ext4 /dev/rbd device distinct from the container root. The nondefault NBD canary is not selected.
Init mounts scratch only at /scratch and copies the image-visible /nix and cache into staging. Runner mounts the completed five subdirectories only after init succeeds.
Old attempts are removed, file bytes/counts/symlink counts are compared, the Nix store/var are required, ownership/modes are set, and at least 45Gi remains before publishing the completion marker.

The local generated revision has the same retained live digest in both init and runner for both architectures, and identical init-script bytes. Main source uses its base digest; this is not evidence of a deployed init/runner mismatch.
Retained templates exactly match source minimum 5 / maximum 10, architecture, Pod security context, init resources/mounts and runner resources/mounts. No settings were changed.

phaseInterpretation: Retained MountDevice DeadlineExceeded events occurred before the affected init-scratch containers started. Copy/verification work cannot explain those initial device-mount deadlines. Two selected Pods later progressed to running init; no permanent deadlock was established.
remainingEvidenceLimit: The exact failed CSI/kernel-RBD operation and underlying device/network/backend cause are not established by these manifests or retained event reasons. This source-only audit does not justify changing runner counts, storage, durability, mount timeouts or admission checks.
limitations: Atlas context did not match the owned checkout; stale historical notes were not used as current facts. Exact Git objects and retained live field comparison were used instead.
The generated revision is a locally retained Git object whose relevant content matches retained live image/template fields; no new claim about current Argo revision was queried.
No new Kubernetes, metric, log, database, cache or Pod-exec read; no load test, repository edit, runner mutation or policy change was performed.
